description: a coordinator hands one batch per round to 4 workers and waits for all of them; worker-2 commits results under cache_lock, which a flusher thread also takes every round

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: holder_sleeps
faults.summary: the flusher holds cache_lock across a 40 ms sleep every round; worker-2 blocks on cache_lock (futex) and every round waits for worker-2 (batch_server <- worker-2 <- flusher <- timer)

faults.name: contention
faults.summary: each worker, on its own CPU, does its 5 ms as 40 short critical sections on one shared stats_lock, so the workers keep blocking on each other for short futex waits

faults.name: convoy
faults.summary: each worker, on its own CPU, holds one global lock for its whole 5 ms of work, so the four workers run one after another instead of in parallel

faults.name: deadlock
faults.summary: at 40% of the run, worker-1 takes lock A then B while worker-3 takes B then A; both block forever, and the coordinator waits forever for the round

faults.name: hang
faults.summary: at 40% of the run, worker-3 blocks forever reading a pipe nobody writes to; the coordinator waits forever for the round (no lock cycle)

faults.name: priority_inversion
faults.summary: on one CPU: worker-2 (SCHED_FIFO 10) needs cache_lock, held by the flusher (FIFO 1), which is preempted by the compactor (FIFO 5) burning 15 ms; worker-2 waits for the medium-priority thread

description: a sampler thread runs every 2 ms (0.2 ms of work per cycle) and an uploader thread wakes every 500 ms

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: one_off_delay
faults.summary: once, at 50% of the run, the maintenance thread (SCHED_FIFO 10, same CPU) spins for 30 ms; the sampler wakes ~30 ms late once

faults.name: jitter
faults.summary: all run long, the maintenance thread (SCHED_FIFO 10, same CPU) spins 0.3-1.8 ms at random every 0.5-2.5 ms; the sampler's wake-up lateness varies from 0 to ~1.8 ms

faults.name: gradual_slowdown
faults.summary: the sampler's work per cycle grows steadily from 0.1 ms to 3 ms over the run, so its cycles stretch and, past ~65% of the run, overrun the 2 ms period

faults.name: sudden_change
faults.summary: at 50% of the run the sampler's work per cycle jumps from 0.2 ms to 2.5 ms, so every later cycle overruns the 2 ms period

faults.name: oversleeping
faults.summary: the sampler's timer slack is 4 ms (prctl PR_SET_TIMERSLACK), so its 2 ms-period sleeps end up to 4 ms late

faults.name: rt_preempted
faults.summary: the sampler runs at SCHED_FIFO 20; every 300 ms the maintenance thread (SCHED_FIFO 50, same CPU) spins for 5 ms and preempts it

description: every 100 ms a coordinator gives 8 calc threads (one per CPU) 10 ms of CPU work each and waits for all of them

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: load_imbalance
faults.summary: calc-0 gets 4x the work (40 ms per round) and the other seven get 10 ms, every round; the others finish early and wait at the barrier for calc-0

faults.name: barrier_straggler
faults.summary: every calc thread gets the same 10 ms of work, but a monitor thread (SCHED_FIFO 10) on calc-5's CPU spins 20 ms at the start of every round, so calc-5 is runnable but waiting and finishes last; everyone waits for it at the barrier

faults.name: cpu_hog
faults.summary: an indexer thread uses 100% of one CPU (its own) for the whole run

faults.name: busy_wait
faults.summary: a collector thread spin-waits on a flag (no syscalls) for each round's results instead of blocking: 100% of one CPU, almost all of it waiting

faults.name: cpu_starvation
faults.summary: every 5 s a monitor thread (SCHED_FIFO 10) on calc-3's CPU spins for 2 s; calc-3 is runnable but barely runs, and its rounds stretch to ~1 s

faults.name: oversubscription
faults.summary: 32 calc threads share 4 CPUs (the healthy run has 8 threads on 8 CPUs), each with 10 ms of work per round; they wait in the run queues

faults.name: migrations
faults.summary: each calc thread moves itself to the next CPU (sched_setaffinity) after every 1 ms of work: ~800 migrations per second

faults.name: odd_worker
faults.summary: calc-6 also writes 200 small log lines (write(), 64 bytes each) after its CPU work, every round; the other calc threads only compute

description: a record store: a writer appends a 4 KB record every 5 ms and syncs every 2 s, a reader reads 64 KB every 100 ms, and a stats thread checks the file once a second

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: disk_wait
faults.summary: the writer syncs every record: 1000 records per second, each written and then fdatasync()ed (~0.6 ms on the disk each), plus an 8 MB checkpoint synced once a second (several ms); the writer is blocked on the disk 35-50% of the time

faults.name: small_calls
faults.summary: every 100 ms the reader reads 5000 bytes one byte per read() call (~50,000 read calls per second) instead of one 64 KB read

faults.name: polling
faults.summary: the stats thread calls poll() with a zero timeout on a pipe that never has data, then sleeps 200 us, over and over (~4000 polls per second, all returning nothing)

faults.name: retry_loop
faults.summary: the stats thread tries to open data/incoming/batch.ready every 1 ms; the file never exists, so every open() fails with ENOENT

faults.name: file_churn
faults.summary: the writer writes each 4 KB record to a new file (create, write, close, rename) and deletes the file from 100 records earlier: ~200 files created and deleted per second

faults.name: unexpected_scan
faults.summary: every 2 s the stats thread walks /usr/share/doc, opening and reading the start of up to 300 files that have nothing to do with the store

description: reader -> parser -> 4 sinks joined by bounded queues; 2000 items per second

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: slow_stage
faults.summary: the parser spends 1.5 ms per item instead of 0.2 ms, below the reader's 2000 items per second: its input queue stays full, the reader blocks on it and the sinks starve

faults.name: bursty
faults.summary: the reader produces in bursts, 500 items as fast as it can, then nothing for 400 ms: the queues fill up during a burst and drain empty between bursts

faults.name: herd
faults.summary: 16 sink threads (instead of 4) share one queue, and the parser wakes all of them (pthread_cond_broadcast) for every item: each item wakes 16 threads and only one gets it

faults.name: idle_workers
faults.summary: the parser hands every item to sink-0 instead of round-robin: sink-0 is busy ~80% of the time and sink-1..3 never get any work

faults.name: idle_thread
faults.summary: an extra compressor thread is started at launch and waits forever for work that never comes; the pipeline itself is healthy

description: 4 client threads each send a request every 5 ms over loopback TCP to a key-value server process (kvd) and wait for the reply

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: slow_backend
faults.summary: the server (process kvd) spends 3 ms per request instead of 0.1 ms, all on one CPU: the server is saturated and the clients spend most of their time blocked waiting for its replies

faults.name: tail_latency
faults.summary: 2% of requests, chosen at random, take 25 ms on the server (a slow path that waits) instead of 0.1 ms; the other 98% are as fast as in the healthy run

faults.name: network_wait
faults.summary: once a second each client tries to reach a replica at 10.255.255.1:7070, which never answers, and waits 300 ms for the connection before giving up: the clients are blocked on the network ~30% of the time

description: an in-memory cache: a 256 MB arena filled at start, a loader that refreshes part of it every 200 ms, and two server threads doing lookups every 1 ms

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: memory_pressure
faults.summary: every 200 ms the loader discards the whole 256 MB arena (madvise MADV_DONTNEED) and touches every page again, four times over: ~260,000 page faults per cycle, keeping the loader busy about a quarter of the time, almost all of it in the kernel handling them

faults.name: allocation_churn
faults.summary: for every lookup batch the servers allocate a 256 KB buffer, fill it and free it; each allocation is an mmap() and each free an munmap() (~1000 of each per second per server)

description: a dispatcher queues a 2 ms CPU job every 10 ms for a pool of 4 job threads

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: slow_startup
faults.summary: before running any job, start-up spends 1.5 s of CPU on initialisation and then waits 1.5 s: the first job runs ~3 s after the start (the healthy start-up takes ~20 ms)

faults.name: slow_shutdown
faults.summary: at the end of the run each job thread, one after another, holds a shared lock for 1.5 s while it flushes its state: the process takes ~6 s to exit after its last job

faults.name: crash
faults.summary: every 5 s the dispatcher forks a helper process (job-helper) for a batch; the third helper dies of a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) instead of exiting normally; the dispatcher carries on

faults.name: fork_storm
faults.summary: every job runs a short-lived process (fork + exec of /usr/bin/true) instead of running in the pool thread: ~100 processes started per second

faults.name: thread_churn
faults.summary: every job runs on a brand-new thread, created and joined by the dispatcher, instead of the pool: ~100 threads created per second

faults.name: never_exits
faults.summary: at 40% of the run all jobs are done and the dispatcher shuts the pool down, but job-2 is blocked forever reading a pipe nobody writes to, so the process never exits; it sits idle until the end of the run

description: a render thread produces a report every 50 ms (8 ms of CPU work) on one CPU

faults.name: none
faults.summary: no fault: the program's healthy baseline

faults.name: neighbour
faults.summary: from 30% to 80% of the run a separate process, indexd, runs three CPU-bound threads on the render thread's CPU; render only gets a quarter of its CPU and each report takes ~4x longer

faults.name: irq_storm
faults.summary: from 30% to 70% of the run an archive thread on render's CPU re-reads stored reports with direct 4 KB reads, 64 in flight; their completion interrupts land on render's CPU, taking about a fifth of it, and each report takes longer
